title: [Next14] Phase in next config is set to `PHASE_DEVELOPMENT_SERVER` when running `next build`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

labels.name: linear: next
labels.description: Confirmed issue that is tracked by the Next.js team.

body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/great-cdn-k9f434

### To Reproduce

1. Run the build script in the linked reproduction sandbox
2. Observe the logged output for the phase values

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current behavior**
Starting with next.js v14, it seems that the next config is loaded twice when running `next build`:

- The first time, the `phase` value is set to `PHASE_PRODUCTION_BUILD` and the invocation is triggered by https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/1c5d7782a02259007a101124f6774d0251c7d3ff/packages/next/src/build/index.ts#L372
- The second time, the `phase` value is set to `PHASE_DEVELOPMENT_SERVER` and the invocation is triggered by `getStartServerInfo` in https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/1c5d7782a02259007a101124f6774d0251c7d3ff/packages/next/src/build/index.ts#L514. It seems that `getStartServerInfo` always uses `PHASE_DEVELOPMENT_SERVER`, no matter the context: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/1c5d7782a02259007a101124f6774d0251c7d3ff/packages/next/src/server/lib/app-info-log.ts#L58

**Expected behavior**
`getStartServerInfo` should be called with a value of `PHASE_PRODUCTION_BUILD` when run in a `next build` context.

In my case, I used the `phase` value to skip the execution of some logic only in the buildphase which is now no longer possible.
I worked around this issue by using a custom env var when launching the build`BUILD_PHASE=true next build` and then checking for the value of this env var in my `next.config.js`. 

I wonder if this change is intended behaviour or a bug. In my opinion, the `phase` argument loses most of its usefulness if it's set this way.



### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: x64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 22.6.0: Fri Sep 15 13:39:52 PDT 2023; root:xnu-8796.141.3.700.8~1/RELEASE_X86_64
Binaries:
  Node: 20.9.0
  npm: 10.1.0
  Yarn: 1.22.19
  pnpm: N/A
Relevant Packages:
  next: 14.0.2-canary.6
  eslint-config-next: 14.0.1
  react: 18.2.0
  react-dom: 18.2.0
  typescript: 5.2.2
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```


### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Not sure

### Additional context

I use a custom server for my next.js app. However, the example repo I linked for reproduction suffers from the same issue and does not use a custom server.
